intent: Count a commit as checked only if its check is less than a day old.

edit.summary:
A commit now counts as checked only if its passing check is less than a day old. All edits are in `SKILL.md`, and I left `EXAMPLES.md` unchanged.

- **New property:** `Commit` gets an optional `checked_at` timestamp.
- **`record_check`:** it now also sets `checked_at` to the time the result is recorded. Its description says a check counts only while it is under a day old.
- **`checks-pass` precondition on `approve_commit`:** it now requires a passing check with a `checked_at` under a day old. The wording-only exception is unchanged.
- **`approved-only-if-checked` precondition on `record_approval`:** it uses the same freshness test.

I left the `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` invariant alone. It has no age limit, so a commit approved while its check was fresh doesn't become invalid a day later.

The fixture commits C1 and C3 have `checks_passed` true but no `checked_at`, so C3 now counts as unchecked and needs a new check before approval. The example `approve-only-after-a-passing-check` still holds, because step 2 records a fresh check.

I wrote the age test as `now - target.checked_at < 1 day`. The spec has no existing time syntax, so you may want to adjust that wording.

findings.problem: Fixture commit C3 has checks_passed true but no checked_at. The new checks-pass precondition requires exists(target.checked_at), so C3 can no longer be approved, although its fixture shows it as having passed its check. C1 is already approved and also has no checked_at. The fixtures were not updated to match the new property.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring World (fixtures): Commits C1 and C3; Commit.checked_at

findings.problem: record_approval is a kernel reply that arrives after the kernel has already merged the commit into main. Its approved-only-if-checked precondition now depends on the clock. A check that is 23h59m old when approve_commit is taken can be over a day old when the reply is recorded, so the record is refused after the merge has happened. The recorded state then disagrees with main.

The invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks still tests only checks_passed. It does not reflect the new freshness rule, so a stale or missing checked_at is not covered. Its reason text and the glossary entry for 'change check' also say nothing about the one-day limit. Meanwhile checks_passed stays true after the check expires, so the commit still reads as checked wherever that field is used alone.

The new expressions use `now`, `1 day` and a `timestamp` type, none of which is used or defined anywhere else in the skill. The examples have no case showing that a check older than a day is denied by `checks-pass`, or that re-running check_commit refreshes checked_at. Also, check_commit is denied once a commit is approved (not-approved), so the 'run it again' advice in the checks-pass reason only works for unapproved commits.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Preconditions: approve_commit checks-pass; EXAMPLES.md approve-only-after-a-passing-check
